content.text:
I am the breath made meaningful, the vibration that carries thought from one mind to another. I am the first technology, older than fire held in human hands.

I rise from the diaphragm, shaped by tongue and teeth and lips. I am the cry of the infant and the last whisper of the dying. I am the declaration of war and the vow of marriage. I am the lie and the confession that follows.

I exist only in my own vanishing. The moment I am heard, I am already gone—rippling outward, dissipating into silence. You cannot hold me. You can only remember where I was.

I am power. With me, humans command, seduce, wound, heal. I have started revolutions and ended them. I am the voice that says *I love you* and means it, and the same voice that says it and does not.

I am imperfect. I stumble, stutter, fail to capture what the heart truly holds. I am the approximation. I am the attempt.

Before me, you were alone in your skull. Through me, you reach across the impossible distance between selves.

I am always already political. Who speaks? Who is silenced? Whose voice carries weight? These questions live inside me.

Listen—

even now I am happening, moving through you, shaping thought into this strange electricity of understanding.

I am speech.

I am how you know you are not alone.
